$ rea --help

--- stdout
rea@<version> — Reverse engineer anything from your terminal or agent.

Usage: rea <command>

Commands:
  address-to-file-offset  Map one analysis address to a file offset; memory bytes may differ and ranges may not be contiguous
  <registered command rows elided>
  build-reconstruction-obligation-ledger  Generate a deterministic Evidence-backed reconstruction obligation ledger page
  <registered command rows elided>
  decompile  Read one part of an app as code. Supply at least one of the positional address or --procedure. Alternatively, use --file-offset alone. Equal positional and --procedure values are accepted; conflicts fail. With Ghidra, a space-qualified address such as ram:0x... avoids file-offset fallback; inspect-native-load-image reports the observed default space.
  <registered command rows elided>
  inspect-byte-entropy  Inspect file-wide and block byte entropy without executing the file
  <registered command rows elided>
  setup  Configure agent integrations and optional analysis providers
  <registered command rows elided>
  xrefs  List bounded, untyped references to an analyzed address. For typed incoming references, use inspect-native-instruction at the target address where supported. Supply at least one of the positional address or --address. Equal values are accepted; conflicts fail.

Integrations:
  completions  Generate shell completion script
  mcp          Register as MCP server (add, doctor)

Custom Global Options:
  --timings  Write measured command timing to stderr.

Global Options:
  --filter-output <keys>                      Filter output by key paths (e.g. foo,bar.baz,a[0,3])
  --format <toon|json|yaml|md|jsonl|csv|tsv>  Output format
  --full-output                               Show full output envelope
  --help                                      Show help
  --json                                      Shorthand for --format json
  --llms, --llms-full                         Print LLM-readable manifest
  --mcp                                       Start as MCP stdio server
  --schema                                    Show JSON Schema for command
  --token-count                               Print token count of output (instead of output)
  --token-limit <n>                           Limit output to n tokens
  --token-offset <n>                          Skip first n tokens of output
  --update                                    Update to latest version
  --version                                   Show version
<end>
